synopsis.body: The widest error bars on the card, by some way. The model backs an undefeated fighter with ten minutes of UFC time (trust 0.152) over a 231-point Elo favourite, and the engines disagree violently: hand-tuned 50.9%, GBM 75.0%. Most of the gap comes from correcting his pre-UFC record from a 0-0 placeholder to his real 11-0, which alone moved this fight +10.0pp. The bear case for Klose is real — he beat Barboza last time — but he is 38.5, has been finished in 67% of his losses, and has been inactive 386 days. Size the position for the uncertainty, not the percentage.

matchupAnalysis: Garcia 53.6% in the closest fight on the card, and one that flipped during preparation: Rongzhu's pre-UFC record was a 0-0 placeholder until this run, and restoring his real 21-3 (14 KO, 5 submission) moved the fight 6.0 points toward Garcia. That direction is counter-intuitive and worth stating plainly — giving the model more evidence about Rongzhu did not flatter him. Note also that Garcia holds the card's largest Elo edge in this pairing (+278, 1937 to 1659) while the hand-tuned layer disagrees, favouring Rongzhu at 58.1% against the GBM's 48.6%.

The stylistic split is clean. Rongzhu is the striker: power +0.75, output +0.59, 6.05 strikes per minute, 45.1% head-strike accuracy and 84.5% takedown defence, on a three-fight win streak. Garcia is the grappler: grappling +0.60, wrestling defence +0.94, 0.215 takedowns per minute and a +0.163 control differential, with power at -0.37 and a slightly negative strike differential. He is also on a three-fight run of his own — Alexander Hernandez, Jared Gordon and Vinc Pichel — and against a notably stronger schedule, which the strength-of-schedule multipliers capture: 1.148 for Garcia against 0.860 for Rongzhu, the largest such gap here.

The durability numbers are where Garcia's edge quietly compounds. Rongzhu's finished rate is 0.667 against Garcia's 0.250, and his last defeat was a doctor's stoppage against Chris Padilla. This projects as much the longest fight on the card: decisions 65.2%, Over 1.5 at 77.4% and Over 2.5 at 68.3% — both the highest three-round totals here. That fits two fighters who mostly go the distance, and it means the value in this matchup is likelier to sit in the totals market than the moneyline, where a 53.6/46.4 split offers very little.

synopsis.body: Narrowly — the tightest projection on the card at 53.6/46.4, and a fight that flipped when Rongzhu's pre-UFC record was corrected from a 0-0 placeholder to 21-3 — which moved it 6.0pp toward Garcia, not away. Garcia brings the grappling (+0.60), the wrestling defence (+0.94), the far stronger schedule (SoS 1.148 vs 0.860) and much better durability (finished in 25% of losses against Rongzhu's 67%). The engines split — hand-tuned 58.1% for Rongzhu, GBM 48.6% — so take the moneyline lightly and note the card-high totals: Over 2.5 at 68.3%.

matchupAnalysis: Belgaroui 71.2%, and this fight carries both the card's largest Elo gap (+320, 1827 to 1507) and its largest engine disagreement — hand-tuned 94.2% against a GBM reading of 72.2%, a 22-point spread. The hand-tuned case is almost absurdly one-sided on composites: Belgaroui's output is +2.64 and his power +1.14, his KO finish rate is 1.000 with three consecutive knockouts (Iwasaki, Bekoev, Abdul-Malik), and his strike differential is +3.93 per minute on 56.7% head-strike accuracy — the best accuracy figure on the card. Santos's power sits at -0.69 and his finish rate is 0.000.

The GBM's much more restrained number is the one to work from, and the reasons are visible. Belgaroui has four UFC fights and 52 minutes of cage time, so his trust is 0.745 and those spectacular rates are still being shrunk. He is 34.3 with an age factor of 0.943. And his one blemish — a decision loss to Marco Tulio — is the only time he has been taken past the first exchange in the UFC, which is a thin basis for judging how he handles adversity. Santos, meanwhile, is not a soft touch structurally: his wrestling defence is +0.86, his takedown defence 85.0%, and his chin +0.35 against a background of never having been knocked out.

Where Santos loses is in threat generation. He has no finishes at all in four UFC fights, his most recent outing was a submission loss to Baisangur Susurkaev, and his finished rate of 0.500 says that when he does lose, it tends to be conclusive. Belgaroui also holds a substantial physical edge — 200.66cm of reach against 190.5, a +1.97 versus -0.04 composite split. The sim splits the difference sensibly: a 26.2% KO share for Belgaroui but decisions still the plurality outcome at 57.3%, with Over 2.5 at 61.0%.

synopsis.body: The card's biggest Elo gap (+320) and its biggest engine disagreement (hand-tuned 94.2%, GBM 72.2%) — trust the GBM. Belgaroui's numbers are genuinely excellent (output +2.64, a 1.000 KO finish rate, a +3.93 strike differential, 200.66cm of reach) but rest on four UFC fights and 52 minutes, shrunk to trust 0.745, at age 34.3. Santos defends well (85.0% takedown defence, +0.86 wrestling defence) but generates nothing — zero finishes in four UFC fights. 71.2% is the honest middle.

matchupAnalysis: Tarin 58.6%, and this projection needs its caveats read before its number. Tarin is billed under a name the dataset does not use — ufcstats stores her as Regina Malpica Rivera — and she has exactly one UFC bout, a Catch Weight decision over Ernesta Kareckaite in February. Her trust is 0.214, so her composites are pinned close to the flyweight mean and none of them should be read as measurements. Two displayed figures are outright artefacts: her Elo of 1500 is the cold-start default, not an earned rating (she has zero divisional fights), and her reach composite of +1.96 is computed from a default 180cm, because fighter_data holds no measured reach or height for her at all.

What is real is her record and her age. She is 8-0, and her pre-UFC ledger — another of the five placeholder rows corrected before this run — is 7-0 with four knockouts and two submissions across the Mexican regional circuit. At 21.9 she is by some distance the youngest fighter on the card. The pre-UFC features are precisely the mechanism the model uses for fighters with no UFC sample, and correcting her row moved this fight materially. That is the model working as designed, but it is also the model reasoning almost entirely from a record rather than from observed UFC performance.

Aldrich is the known quantity and the profile is a modest one. Over 17 UFC fights she carries an output composite of -0.33, a negative strike differential (-0.42 per minute), a finish rate of 0.091 — one finish in eleven wins — and a finishing ability modifier of 0.091. She is 33.9 with an age factor of 0.953 and a chin-damage modifier of 0.861, though she does arrive on a two-fight win streak (Jamey-Lyn Horth, Andrea Lee). The hand-tuned layer, which leans on composites, has this near even at 53.7% for Aldrich; the GBM, which can weigh the records, sits at 41.6%. The fight projects as the most likely on the card to go to the judges — 67.6% decisions, Over 2.5 at 71.8%.

synopsis.body: Held loosely: an 8-0 21-year-old with one UFC bout (trust 0.214) is favoured over a 17-fight veteran, and the engines disagree: hand-tuned 53.7% for Aldrich, GBM 41.6%. The case is her corrected 7-0 pre-UFC record (4 KO, 2 submission) against Aldrich's genuinely thin output — a -0.33 output composite, a negative strike differential and one finish in eleven wins. Two numbers in Tarin's column are artefacts and should be ignored: her 1500 Elo is a cold-start default and her +1.96 reach is built on a default 180cm, not a measurement. Expect a decision (67.6%).
